title: While studying for UPSC, should one subject be done at one go or should subjects be combined and studied?
reason: The user is asking about study methodology and time management between subjects. The provided notes on Optional Strategy and Prelims strategy (active recall vs. binge-reading) directly address how to structure a study plan to ensure conceptual depth and consistency.

matched_note.title: UPSC Optional Subject Strategy, Syllabus Overlap, Resource Selection & Time Allocation

drafted_comment:
The real issue here is avoiding 'binge-reading' where you finish one book but forget 80% of it by next week. For UPSC, a hybrid approach works best to maintain momentum.

1. Use a Balanced Daily Split: During your foundation phase, try allocating about 60% of your time to your Optional and 40% to GS and Current Affairs. This prevents you from falling behind on General Studies while mastering your core subject.
2. Prioritize Active Recall: Instead of finishing a whole subject at once, study a topic and immediately solve 5-10 syllabus-aligned MCQs. This yields much higher retention than just reading pages.
3. Focus on Overlap: Choose subjects that share syllabus overlap to save time.
